historical_references.reference: Bhoomitha Devi, also known as Prithvi Devi or Prithvi Goddess, is a Hindu goddess worshipped as the goddess of the earth. She is the wife of Vishnu in his Avatar as Vamana. The legend of Vamana is mentioned in the Mahabharata and Puranas. In this story, Vamana, disguised as a dwarf, asks King Mahabali for three paces of land. Mahabali, in his generosity, grants this wish. Vamana then grows to his true size and covers the three worlds. Bhoomitha Devi is the earth that Vamana steps on during this expansion.

Bhoomitha or Prithvi is also considered the primary wife of Rudra, the god of destruction, in the Shiva Purana. In this context, Prithvi is described as the earth, the goddess who forms the basis of all existence and sustains all living beings. She is said to have emerged from the navel of Brahma, the creator of the universe, and is often depicted as a throne for Shiva, symbolizing his connection to the earth and its manifestations.
